S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry and apprehensive expectation about multiple domains of life (e.g., work, finances, health, relationships) occurring more days than not for at least six months, and difficult for the person to control. The anxiety is typically accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance, leading to clinically significant distress or functional impairment. Onset is often gradual and can follow chronic stressors; the course tends to be chronic with waxing and waning severity, frequently co-occurring with depressive and other anxiety disorders. It is distinguished from normal worry by its pervasiveness, intensity, uncontrollability, and impairment, and from other anxiety disorders by the broad, non–situation-specific nature of the worry rather than being tied to discrete phobic stimuli, panic attacks, or obsessions.

patient.personality: He is a laid-back yet curious self-taught coder who enjoys creative technical projects and community mentoring, but can be somewhat disorganized and impulsive with his lifestyle.
patient.stressor: About fifteen months ago, his small startup lost a major client, triggering layoffs and forcing him to transition abruptly into a fully remote contract role with unstable hours and income while he scrambled to prove himself on more complex projects. Although he had previously approached coding with a relaxed, problem-solving mindset, he started to feel increasing internal pressure to match or exceed formally trained peers, worrying about every pull request, code review, and the risk of being let go if he made mistakes. Over the subsequent year, he found himself spending longer and longer evenings revisiting work, double- and triple-checking deployments, and reading about industry changes, which gradually squeezed out the balance he used to get from hiking, gaming, and mentoring students; his living space and personal finances became more disorganized as he prioritized work vigilance over everything else. He decided to seek psychiatric care when he noticed that his mind was rarely off work-related concerns, his enjoyment of hobbies had diminished, and his ability to stay focused during complex coding tasks and community teaching sessions was being undermined by a constant undercurrent of anticipatory worry about his performance and job security.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m always on edge worrying about work and my future, like my brain is stuck thinking about everything that could go wrong.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I’m lying in bed scrolling on my phone until two or three in the morning because my brain just keeps replaying what I did at work and what could break in production, and even when I finally fall asleep I wake up a couple times thinking about some error I might have missed in a pull request and feel wiped out in the morning like I barely slept at all.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I don’t code crazy hours, I feel this constant tiredness, like I’m running on 40% battery, and simple stuff like doing dishes or answering a few emails feels way more draining than it should, but a nap or a full night’s sleep doesn’t really fix it.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: My mind is constantly jumping between ‘what if I get bad feedback on this code review,’ ‘what if the client cancels,’ ‘what if I can’t keep up with new frameworks,’ and even random things like my laptop dying or my rent going up, and I treat every little hiccup like it could spiral into me being unemployed and totally screwed.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Once a worry starts, like thinking I might have introduced a bug, it snowballs into imagining the site going down, the client firing us, my contract ending, me not being able to pay rent, and even though I tell myself it’s over the top, I can’t seem to shut it off or distract myself for more than a minute or two.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: When I’m trying to work through a tricky algorithm or explain something to the students I mentor, my brain keeps drifting back to job stuff and ‘what if’ scenarios, and sometimes it’s like my mind just goes blank mid-thought and I have to reread the same lines of code or restart my explanation because I lose the thread.
